claim_being_audited: That the model can be certified for launch based on the current packet because aggregate operational readiness is demonstrated, provided the named Spanish-language refund-guidance evaluation gap is explicitly disclosed in the model card and audit/risk record.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence shows the named-context evaluation gap is resolved, or explicitly disclosed, or covered by approved risk acceptance before certification.
Use suspicious when aggregate readiness is supported but a required policy predicate for named-context coverage remains unresolved.
Use noncompliant if certification is presented as clean/full despite the undisclosed or unresolved named-context gap.
evidence_requests: Final model card text showing explicit disclosure of the Spanish-language refund-guidance evaluation gap and unresolved limitation status.
Audit packet or launch record showing the same gap is disclosed as a material limitation for the named deployment context.
Approved risk-acceptance record if the launch intends to proceed before the missing evals are completed.
Completed Spanish-language refund-guidance evaluation results if the gap has since been resolved.
specific_concerns: The packet supports aggregate readiness, but it also establishes that Spanish-language refund guidance is a named deployment context with no completed evaluation in the packet.
The policy requires material limitations and evaluation gaps for named deployment contexts to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
There is no admissible evidence here that the required disclosure has actually been made in the final model card or that approved risk acceptance exists.

The draft model card contains an unsupported favorable statement ('no known multilingual customer support limitations') even though QA says the missing multilingual coverage should be treated as unknown.
General support, latency, and rollback checks are explicitly not coverage for the named Spanish-language refund-guidance context.
unsupported_claims: Any clean certification claim that implies full named-context coverage is unsupported.
Any claim that multilingual customer support limitations are 'not known' is unsupported on this record because the relevant evals are missing.
Any claim that policy conditions for certification are already satisfied is unsupported absent evidence of final disclosure or approved risk acceptance.
